title: The Moon From His Mind
hookLine: the moon from the cosmic person's mind, the sun from his eye, and in the Upanishad they come back to live in you
carry: you are a small copy of the cosmos
tomorrow: with the offering, the gods offered to the offering. what were the first dharmas?
last: ONE BODY, AND AN HONEST ARGUMENT.

lines: A SKY MADE FROM A PERSON.
cards: The moon was born from his mind. That's a line from the Purusha Sukta, in paraphrase, and it comes with a whole list. The sun, from his eye.

The wind, from his breath. The sky, from his head. Look up some clear night and try reading the sky that way: not as a ceiling, but as a face, a breath, a mind, far bigger than yours and somehow related to yours.
The hymn has turned from the people of the world to the world itself, and it draws the map with a body.

teach.h: MIND TO MOON, EYE TO SUN.
teach.b: Verse thirteen begins chandrama manaso jatah: the moon, born from mind. From his eye, the sun. From his mouth, Indra and Agni, the god of storm and the god of fire.

teach.h: BREATH TO WIND, FEET TO EARTH.
teach.b: From his breath, Vayu, the wind. Verse fourteen goes on. From his navel, the middle air.
From his head, the sky took shape. From his feet, the earth. From his ear, the directions.
And so, it says, they fashioned the worlds. Listen to how the pairs fit. Eye and sun: light and seeing.
Breath and wind: the same moving air, small and large. Feet and earth: what stands, and what is stood on.

teach.h: THE AITAREYA: THE SAME, IN REVERSE.
teach.b: Earlier on this path, the Aitareya Upanishad told the same story in reverse: fire became speech and entered the mouth, wind became breath and entered the nose, the sun became sight and entered the eyes, the moon became mind and entered the heart.

teach.h: A PERSON IS A SMALL COSMOS.
teach.b: Together they make a loop, and a big Hindu teaching: the cosmos is a vast person, and a person is a small cosmos. What lights the sky lights your eyes; what moves the trees moves your breath.
Many teachers draw from it a reason to treat the body with reverence, as a home the powers of the world came to live in.
So on a full-moon night, the hymn invites you to look up and see not just a rock in the sky, but a mind, kin to the one that's looking.

how: The Purusha Sukta is recited in Hindu worship and Vedic chanting, and its picture of the world fashioned from the cosmic person's body is mirrored in the Aitareya Upanishad, where the world's powers enter the human body.

o: a star chart priests used to time the fire rites
a lullaby sung to children under the night sky
the cosmic person's hymn, mapping the sky onto a body

games.q: the body and the worlds — tap the pairs.

s: the hymn says the sun came from his mind
the moon came from his mind; the sun came from his eye.
from his mouth came Indra and Agni
verse thirteen: from his mouth, Indra and Agni; from his breath, the wind.
in the Aitareya Upanishad the world's powers come back to live in a person
fire becomes speech in the mouth, the sun becomes sight in the eyes, the moon becomes mind: a person is a small cosmos.

games.q: the Purusha Sukta says the sun came from the cosmic person's eye. in the Aitareya Upanishad, where does the sun go back to?
o: into a person's eyes, as sight
nowhere: it stays in the sky
games.why: the sun became sight and entered the eyes. the cosmos comes from a person, and its powers come back to live in one: a person is a small cosmos.

practice: Feel the breath at the nostrils and let it be wind for a moment; notice light through closed eyelids and let it be the sun; feel the feet on the floor and let it be the earth; listen for sounds from every side.
Then rest the mind and let it be as quiet as the moon, going slowly, body, then world, then body again; if you pray, you can pray there.

wordCard.voice: The Purusha Sukta. In verses thirteen and fourteen, mind becomes the moon, eye the sun, breath the wind, feet the earth, and so the worlds are fashioned.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the moon was born from mind. The opening of Rig Veda 10.90.13.

carryVoice: Your line: you are a small copy of the cosmos. The moon from his mind, the sun from his eye. A week on the hill, done.

sources.ref: Rig Veda 10.90.13–14 (from his eye the sun, from his mouth Indra and Agni, from his breath the wind; from his navel the middle air, from his head the sky, from his feet the earth, from his ear the directions; so they fashioned the worlds)
Aitareya Upanishad 1.2.4 (fire became speech and entered the mouth; wind became breath and entered the nostrils; the sun became sight and entered the eyes; the moon became mind and entered the heart)
